title: TE James A. Jones, Jr., et al. v. Louisiana Presbytery
disposition_detail: The SJC answered both issues yes, sustained the complaint, annulled Louisiana Presbytery’s April 21, 2007 denial of the complaint, and held that Central Carolina Presbytery’s memorial remained before the SJC, with additional amends stated in 2006-2.
first_summary: Complainants challenged Louisiana Presbytery’s finding of no strong presumption of guilt regarding Steve Wilkins’s teachings. The SJC sustained the complaint, holding that Presbytery used an unduly narrow test requiring express denial or contradiction of the Westminster Standards and failed to independently evaluate identified differences. It annulled Presbytery’s April 21 denial of the complaint and left the Central Carolina Presbytery memorial before the SJC, subject to the additional amends in case 2006-2.
summary: Louisiana Presbytery’s refusal to institute process after examining Steve Wilkins’s Federal Vision teachings was challenged for applying the wrong constitutional standard and overlooking a strong presumption that some views were out of conformity with the Westminster Standards. The SJC sustained the complaint and annulled Presbytery’s denial. A “difference” need not expressly contradict the Standards; Presbytery must independently investigate and classify it rather than accept the member’s assurance or shift the burden to objectors. The ruling did not adjudicate Wilkins’s guilt; the Central Carolina memorial remained before the SJC.
